items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Maybe Dominic was a little, we're good friends, but maybe a little precious because Dominic was from downtown, you see.

ctx.x: It was a company, wasn't it? John Wycliffe.

Yeah, John Wycliffe had the band entertainers. And the Deluxe and the Dreamin' was open. Then you had Jimmy Loom and the Vendome was going big. And Louie was doubling. Later on, before Louie came back, then he doubled from the Vendome. The Vendome to the Sunset. That's when Natty Dominic was playing there with him, you understand? And Dutre. All those bands split up and the men just went like the Four Wings. Dutre was over there with Carol Dixon's band. So I may be in some instances, I may be a little ahead of…

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: And after a while I began to bloom out. And then he began to hire me and Johnny Dots hire me. I recorded with him.

ctx.x: How did you make out in the 50s with Natty Dominic and Baby and those guys?

I did all right. Dominic was another guy. He couldn't see me to begin with. I don't blame the guys. He told, I understand a little Creole or a little French. My people spoke it very well, but I never did pay much attention to it. But I understood what he was saying. He told Al and Omar Simien, what you got this guy for? He can't play. That's what he told him, see. Just like Johnny Dots. But he had to eat it up too. Because I just kept on trying. And after a while I began to bloom out. And then he began to hire me…
When they were giving those slow drag dances in the 1950s. Bill Russell was promoting dances in England. It was Bill who was doing it?
